results.note: ingest/registry.yaml:657 now sets sol_active_addresses expected_update_interval_seconds to 604800 (7 days), down from 86400. The test at tests/test_registry.py:138 asserts that value against the real loaded registry. That matches the workflow's weekly cron, '43 3 * * 0' (.github/workflows/sol-active-addresses.yml:5). The test gate passed.

warn is 691200 (8 days) and stale is 777600 (9 days), set at registry.yaml:658-659. The test asserts warn > interval, stale > warn, and the exact values (lines 139-142). That gives 1 day of headroom before warn and 2 days before stale, replacing the old daily/2-day values.

The test checks every entry except sol_active_addresses and requires each one to still use the standard tier (warn, stale) pair for its interval (300/28800/86400). So no other entry's freshness fields changed. The criterion is met at the registry-entry level, but the diff is not strictly single-file. It also changes ingest/registry.py, adding SUPPORTED_REGISTRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS so the loader accepts 604800. It also edits tests/test_persist_board.py: the daily tier count drops from 55 to 54, and the tier-union test now excludes sol_active_addresses. Neither file is in the declared touch list. The loader change is needed for the YAML to load at all, and the workflow cron was not touched.

The test anchors on a real cron firing time, Sunday 2026-09-27 03:43 UTC. It computes the age one second before the next weekly run (604799s) and asserts that age < the loaded freshness_stale_seconds. That is the same rule the app uses to mark STALE: web/src/data.ts:257 checks `ageSeconds > staleAfterSeconds`, reading the same ingest/registry.yaml (web/src/registry.ts:3). This is weak: the test repeats the comparison in Python instead of calling applyFreshness on a datapoint, and it hardcodes the cron time rather than reading it from the workflow. It still binds the real registry value to the real weekly window.
The `uv run pytest -q` gate exited 0, and the typecheck and test gates also exited 0.

note: The core fix is real and the new tests make meaningful assertions against the loaded registry. Nothing looks faked. Two caveats: the diff also touches ingest/registry.py (loader now allows 604800) and tests/test_persist_board.py (sol_active_addresses no longer counts in the daily tier), neither of which was declared; and the C4 test only checks the thresholds with arithmetic rather than running the app's STALE check (applyFreshness).
